title.narrative: Somalia La Niña-induced Drought Response: strengthening Early Action for Vulnerable Communities in Bay (Baidoa District) and Lower Jubba (Afmadow District)

description.narrative: The proposed project is designed to prioritize severely food-insecure rural women, men, girls, and boys with emergency assistance to save lives and livelihoods. Addressing food insecurity is an urgent action, especially in rural areas with high numbers of people in IPC Phase 4 emergency and IPC Phase 3 crisis. The likelihood of La Niña is now projected at 80%, with early signs already materializing in some regions, leading to drought-induced displacement and worsening protection risks such as family separation and the loss of livestock and livelihood assets. With the looming drought, rural agropastoral communities in Baidoa and Afmadow are reportedly being forced to migrate in search of food and water for humans and pasture for their livestock. The proposed intervention will therefore seek to contribute to providing timely relief by scaling up immediate unconditional cash transfers complemented with emergency livestock inputs to mitigate the impact of the drought that has already started setting in. It will also mitigate drought-induced displacements by providing critical assistance to these rural communities in pre-identified drought hotspot locations.Through this funding, FAO will target 6 250 vulnerable households (approximately 37 500 individuals) to provide treatment for 375 000 animals, including camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, belonging to these households in hard-to-reach and underserved rural areas of Baidoa and Afmadow districts. By protecting livestock, this intervention safeguards the livelihoods of agro-pastoral and pastoral communities, who rely heavily on their animals for enhanced nutrition for under-five children, pregnant and lactating women as well as safeguarding income generated through sales. The animals are “the bank on the hoof” for these vulnerable communities. In addition, FAO will implement its flagship Cash+ approach, which involves providing unconditional cash transfers for 3 months. This will target 1 780 households (10 680 individuals) that are acutely food-insecure and will also benefit from livestock treatment services. Unconditional cash transfers will enable the households to meet their immediate needs and sustain key livestock assets during the harshest dry season. The 1 780 households (10 680 individuals) benefitting from both the cash and the livestock treatment package shall be mobilized and selected based on the food consumption scores and shall target the most vulnerable beneficiaries from the communities using FAO’s approved vulnerability-based targeting criteria.The combined intervention of cash and livestock treatment will meet the immediate needs of the beneficiaries while reducing morbidity, thereby sustaining milk production, especially when little forage is available. Livestock treatment targeting will also benefit neighboring villages and will reduce disease outbreaks that would impact negatively on the animals owned by the very vulnerable communities. Additionally, Somalia Water and Land Information Management (SWALIM) will collect weekly data on strategic water sources, essential for monitoring, analyzing, and projecting Somalia's groundwater situation to support life-saving interventions. This data collected within the first eight weeks of the project, together with information such as the combined drought index, market price monitoring (including water prices) and availability of water provided by Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit (FSNAU) will strengthen the existing early warning systems thus informing relevant drought interventions. SWALIM will deliver critical seasonal weather outlooks and groundwater status to guide prioritization and early action for timely response by both humanitarian and development partners working drought affected districts of Baidoa, (Bay region) and Afmadow (Lower Juba Region).
